gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is the use of the tangential exact-differential integral in place of the normal flux formula. ISSUE-003 instead challenges an unjustified proof step equating a normal derivative flux with an interior integral and requiring a jump/regularity result; it does not identify the tangential-versus-normal formula error.

The gold defect is a wrong plus sign in the complex-layer formula and the resulting false real-part calculation. ISSUE-002 concerns cancellation of boundary integrals in the characteristic-lemma proof when holes meet the fundamental-domain boundary; it does not diagnose the sign or formula error.

The gold defect is the missing quadrature-weight similarity transform in the claimed identity D_s=D^T. ISSUE-005 concerns dropping the additive M term from the Steklov generalized eigenproblem; the formulas, obligations, and failure mechanisms are distinct despite both occurring in numerical implementation.

The gold defect is double application of the quadrature weights in the singular S_1^k block. ISSUE-005 identifies a missing M term in the Steklov pencil, a different matrix and different algebraic operation; its repair does not recognize the singular-block scaling error.

Both identify that the printed Steklov right-hand operator omits the additive M term, so it represents S(I-M) rather than S_0=S(I-M)+M, annihilates constants, and requires the corrected generalized eigenproblem.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Steklov pencil uses the wrong right-hand operator because the +M term in S_0 is omitted; this incorrectly removes the constant-density/zero-mode component and makes the printed problem fail to represent the stated full Steklov problem.

component_coverage.gold_component: The printed right-hand matrix represents S(I-M) instead of the stated modified operator S_0=S(I-M)+M, causing the constant-density subspace and zero Steklov mode to be mishandled.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly states that the +Mφ term is dropped, explains the resulting annihilation of constant vectors and loss of the zero mode, and supplies the corrected pencil with S(I-M)+M.
